about: Suno is a Cambridge, Massachusetts AI music generation company whose platform lets users create full songs with vocals from text prompts. It serves consumers and creators with free and subscription plans, and has tens of millions of users. It raised $250m in November 2025 at a $2.45bn valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and Nvidia's NVentures, and reached a licensing and settlement deal with Warner Music Group. Private. High consumer awareness among online music creators, though also the subject of legal disputes with record labels.

Anchorage Digital is a San Francisco-based regulated crypto custodian and infrastructure firm, holding the first national trust bank charter for digital assets from the US OCC. It provides custody, staking, settlement, trading and tokenisation services to institutions such as crypto funds, banks and corporates. Founded in 2017 and backed by Visa, Andreessen Horowitz, GIC, KKR and others, it was valued at around $3bn after a 2021 round. Private. B2B with limited public awareness, though active in crypto circles.

CDN77 is a content delivery network provider, headquartered in London with operations in Prague, serving video streaming, software downloads and websites through a global network of data centers. Customers include broadcasters, gaming firms, software companies and enterprises, charged by traffic volume and plan. It is owned by Datacamp, the Czech-based infrastructure group, which also runs BunnyCDN competitors and VPN services. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Hyperliquid Strategies is a New York-based digital asset treasury company formed in 2025 to hold the HYPE token of the Hyperliquid decentralised exchange, financed through a roughly $583m private placement and a merger with Sonnet BioTherapeutics, listed on Nasdaq (PURR). Its income depends on the HYPE token's price and any staking returns, and its investors include Paradigm and others. Public vehicle with no products for consumers. Low consumer awareness, but known in crypto investing.

about: Wayflyer is a Dublin-based revenue-based financing and growth platform for e-commerce brands, providing funding for inventory and marketing along with analytics. Customers are online merchants across the US, UK, Europe, Canada and Australia, and Wayflyer earns fees on advances. Founded in 2019, it raised a $150m Series B in 2022 and debt facilities, valued at about $1.6bn, with total funding near $3.7bn including debt. Private. B2B fintech with little consumer awareness.

AlphaSense is a New York market intelligence platform using AI to search and summarise company filings, earnings call transcripts, broker research, news and expert call transcripts. Customers are investment banks, hedge funds, asset managers and large corporations, paying subscriptions, with thousands of enterprise clients and revenue reported above $500m. It acquired Tegus in 2024. Private, valued around $4bn after a 2024 round, backed by Goldman Sachs, Viking and others. B2B, known to finance professionals, not consumers.

Autodesk is a San Francisco software company (legal base in San Francisco, with the Autodesk operations in the Bay Area) selling design and engineering tools such as AutoCAD, Revit, Maya, 3ds Max, Fusion and Autodesk Construction Cloud. Customers are architects, engineers, builders, manufacturers and media creators, paying mainly subscriptions, with revenue near $7bn. Listed on Nasdaq (ADSK). Well known to professionals, including film VFX and automotive design teams, and it has partnered with F1 teams on design technology; not a household consumer brand.

Avalon Labs is described by Crunchbase as a DeFi platform that integrates Bitcoin and other assets into decentralised lending and finance products. The input lists blockchain and cryptocurrency as its industries, shows no HQ country and a placeholder location, and reports funding of about $2.0bn with the latest round in May 2025, a figure that may be inaccurate. Customers and revenue model are not described. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Avalon Labs operates as a DeFi platform that integrates.

about: Axiom Solutions International is listed by Crunchbase as an Austin, Texas company developing digital and electrical products and services, with industries including cloud computing and cloud infrastructure. The input shows funding of about $2.0bn with the latest round in October 2026. The input gives no further detail on its products, customers or ownership, and the name is generic, so identification is uncertain. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Axiom Solutions International develops digital and electrical..

about: Canva is an Australian online design platform, headquartered in Sydney (Surry Hills), whose templates, AI tools and drag-and-drop editor let users make presentations, social posts, videos, documents and print designs. It has over 240 million monthly active users in about 190 countries and an annual revenue above $3bn, earned from Pro, Teams and Enterprise subscriptions. Valued at around $42bn in 2025 secondary share sales. Private, founded 2013 by Melanie Perkins. Very recognisable consumer-and-business brand, with sports and F1 partnership activity including a Mercedes-AMG Petronas tie-up.

CCC Intelligent Solutions is a Chicago cloud platform for the insurance economy, supplying AI-based software for auto claims estimating, repair workflows, parts and total-loss valuation to insurers, repair shops, carmakers and parts suppliers. It links thousands of businesses in the US. Revenue is over $1bn. Listed on the NYSE (CCCS) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Dragoneer Growth Opportunities. B2B, well known to the claims industry, with no consumer brand awareness.

Cyera is a New York AI-native data security platform that discovers, classifies and protects sensitive data across cloud, SaaS and on-premises systems, with data security posture management and access controls. Customers are large enterprises, including Fortune 500 firms. Founded in Israel in 2021, it has raised over $1.7bn including a 2026 round and was valued at about $9bn. Private. B2B cybersecurity brand, known to security teams, with no consumer visibility.

Eurofiber is a Dutch digital infrastructure company based in Maarssen, owning and operating fibre networks in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and France. It sells dark fibre, connectivity, data center interconnect, cloud and managed network services to enterprises, telecoms, government and healthcare customers. Owned by infrastructure funds including Antin and Dutch pension capital after a 2023 funding. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

Figure AI is a San Jose, California AI robotics company building general-purpose humanoid robots, including Figure 02 and Figure 03, together with its Helix vision-language-action model, for use in factories, logistics and eventually homes. It has run pilots with BMW and raised about $1.85bn, valued around $39bn in a 2025 round, with backers including Microsoft, Nvidia, Jeff Bezos, OpenAI and Intel. Private. High profile in technology media; not yet a mainstream consumer brand.

Fireworks AI is a San Mateo, California inference platform that serves open-source and custom AI models quickly and cheaply to developers and enterprises through APIs, fine-tuning and compute services. It was founded in 2022 by former Meta PyTorch engineers, and customers include Uber, Notion, Cursor and Samsung. Funding is about $250m raised at a valuation near $4bn in 2025. Private. B2B developer brand with no consumer awareness.

Flexential is a Centennial, Colorado data center and cloud services provider, operating colocation, managed hosting, cloud, connectivity and disaster recovery services from about 40 data centers across the US. Customers are mid-size and large enterprises and technology firms. It has been owned by GI Partners and Social Capital-style investors, with Churchill Capital-backed ownership since 2021, and is private. B2B infrastructure, no consumer profile.

Isomorphic Labs is a London AI drug discovery company, a sister company of Google DeepMind, founded in 2021 by Demis Hassabis to apply AlphaFold-style models to design new medicines. It has research partnerships with Eli Lilly and Novartis and raised about $600m in 2025 from Thrive Capital, with subsequent funding, owned by Alphabet. Private. Well known in science and tech circles, with no consumer products.

Joulent is listed by Crunchbase as a Houston, Texas company developing large-scale energy systems, and the input places it in artificial intelligence-related industries. Funding shown is about $1.75bn with the latest round in July 2026. The input does not say what products, customers or owners it has, and the name matches no company I can confidently identify. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Macerich is a Santa Monica, California REIT that owns and manages regional shopping centres in major US markets such as Tysons Corner, Scottsdale Fashion Square, Santa Monica Place and Broadway Plaza, leasing space to retailers. Its income is rent and tenant recoveries, and its portfolio holds around 40 malls. Listed on the NYSE (MAC). Property owner, little consumer brand beyond the mall names.

Motive is a San Francisco fleet management and driver safety platform, formerly KeepTruckin, offering AI dashcams, electronic logging devices, vehicle telematics, spend management and compliance tools. It serves tens of thousands of fleets in trucking, construction, oil and gas and field services across North America. Valued at $2.85bn in 2022 and raised around $2bn in total. It filed for a US IPO in 2025. B2B brand, widely seen on truck windshields but not a consumer name.

NEURA Robotics is a Metzingen, Germany robotics company, founded in 2019, making cognitive collaborative robots (the MAiRA and LARA arms) and humanoid robots such as 4NE1, with its Neuraverse platform. It supplies manufacturers and logistics firms, and has a partnership with Kawasaki and Schaeffler. A 2025 round raised about EUR 120m, with later funding reportedly pushing total capital near $1.7bn. Private. Prominent in European tech media, no mainstream consumer brand yet.

Nuro is a Mountain View, California autonomous driving company, founded in 2016, which built small self-driving delivery vehicles before switching to licensing the Nuro Driver technology to automakers and mobility partners. It has a deal with Uber and Lucid to deploy robotaxis. It has raised over $2bn, including a 2021 round that valued it near $8.6bn, from SoftBank, Google and Nvidia. Private. B2B technology brand with moderate awareness in automotive circles.

OpenText is a Waterloo, Ontario enterprise information management software company, selling content management, cybersecurity, analytics, AI and business network products to large enterprises and governments. It grew through acquisitions including Micro Focus (2023) and Carbonite, with revenue near $5bn and about 22,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (OTEX). B2B software company with little consumer awareness, though it has run F1-related and team technology partnerships.

Pinterest is a San Francisco visual discovery platform where users save and organise ideas as pins for shopping, recipes, home, fashion and travel. It has more than 570 million monthly active users and earns from advertising, with revenue near $4bn. Founded in 2010, it listed on the NYSE (PINS) in 2019. Strong consumer social brand with heavy use by women and Gen Z users, and advertiser-focused partnerships rather than sports sponsorship.

Reflection AI is a New York frontier AI lab, founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, working on autonomous coding agents and open frontier models. It raised $2bn in October 2025 at an $8bn valuation, led by Nvidia, with 1789 Capital, Lightspeed and others, and is building up open-weight model releases. Private. Known in AI circles, with no consumer products yet.

Saronic is an Austin, Texas defence technology company building autonomous surface vessels and naval drones for the US Navy and allies, including the Corsair and Marauder vessels, and Port Alpha shipyard in Louisiana. Founded in 2022, it raised $600m in 2025 at a valuation of about $4bn, with later funding reportedly valuing it at around $9bn, from Elad Gil, 8VC, Andreessen Horowitz and others. Private. Government B2B, known in defence tech; not a consumer brand.

SentinelOne is a Mountain View, California cybersecurity company selling its AI-powered Singularity platform for endpoint, cloud, identity and security data protection to businesses and governments worldwide. It reports annual recurring revenue of around $1bn and thousands of customers. Listed on the NYSE (S) since 2021. B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though it has been active in sports sponsorship.

Skild AI is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania robotics AI start-up, formed in 2023 by Carnegie Mellon roboticists, developing a general-purpose robot brain, Skild Brain, to run on many robot types. It raised about $1.4bn in a January 2026 round at a valuation near $14bn, with SoftBank, Nvidia and Macquarie, and earlier backing from Amazon and Lightspeed. Private. Known in AI and robotics circles; no consumer products.

Symrise is a Holzminden, Germany supplier of fragrances, flavours, cosmetic ingredients and pet food ingredients, serving consumer product makers across perfume, personal care, food and beverage and pet food. Revenue is about EUR 5bn with over 12,000 employees. Its brands include Diana Pet Food. Listed in Frankfurt (SY1) in the DAX/MDAX. B2B ingredient firm, so low consumer awareness, though its customers are major consumer brands.

Tabby is a Riyadh-based buy-now-pay-later and fintech company serving the Gulf, with the app offering pay-in-4, instalments, cards and a shopping app across Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait. Founded in the UAE in 2019, it raised $160m in 2025 at a $3.3bn valuation and later reached about $4.5bn in a secondary sale, with Blue Pool, Wellington, PayPal Ventures and others. Private, with a Saudi IPO plan. Strong Gulf consumer brand with heavy advertising and sports sponsorship.

Tempus AI is a Chicago health technology company providing genomic sequencing, clinical data and AI tools for precision medicine, serving oncologists, hospitals and pharma companies running drug development. It holds one of the largest clinical-molecular data libraries, with revenue near $1bn. Founded by Eric Lefkofsky, it listed on Nasdaq (TEM) in June 2024. Mostly B2B and clinician-facing, with modest direct consumer awareness.

Tenable is a Columbia, Maryland cybersecurity company known for the Nessus vulnerability scanner and its Tenable One exposure management platform, covering cloud, identity, operational technology and attack surface. Customers are over 40,000 organizations, including a large part of the Fortune 500, with revenue near $1bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TENB). B2B, with strong awareness in security teams and no consumer brand.

Thinking Machines Lab is a San Francisco AI research and product company founded in 2025 by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, with co-founders including John Schulman. It focuses on collaborative AI systems and released Tinker, a fine-tuning product. It raised $2bn in seed funding in 2025 at a $12bn valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Nvidia and AMD, and has been reported as raising more at a much higher valuation. Private. Heavily covered in tech media; no consumer products yet.

Thomson Reuters is a Toronto-based information and technology company providing legal research (Westlaw), tax and accounting software, news (Reuters) and trade compliance tools to professionals, corporations and governments. It earns subscription revenue of about US$7.3bn and employs about 26,000 people. Majority-controlled by the Thomson family through Woodbridge. Listed on the TSX and Nasdaq (TRI). Mostly B2B, though the Reuters news agency is a globally known brand and it sponsors some events.

Wayve is a London autonomous driving company, founded in 2017, developing end-to-end AI driving software that learns from data rather than high-definition maps. It tests vehicles in the UK, US, Germany and Japan, trialled robotaxis with Uber, and has a deal with Nissan for its ProPilot system. It raised $1.05bn in 2024 (led by SoftBank, with Nvidia and Microsoft) and later raised more, with total funding of about $2.5bn. Private. Well known in tech and mobility circles, with no consumer products yet.

Yondr Group is a London-headquartered developer, owner and operator of hyperscale data centers, building campuses for cloud and technology customers in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific. It was acquired by DigitalBridge in 2021 and later partnered with Ardian. Revenue comes from long-term data center leases. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

Ola (ANI Technologies) is a Bengaluru-based Indian ride-hailing company, with its core cab and auto-rickshaw app, and affiliates including Ola Electric (listed in 2024), Ola Financial Services and Ola Consumer. It serves tens of millions of riders in India. Backed by SoftBank, Tiger Global, Temasek and Matrix, and valued at about $7.3bn in 2021. Private. Very strong brand across Indian cities, with a history in cricket sponsorship, although it has been losing share to Uber and Rapido.

Fireblocks is a New York digital asset infrastructure firm, founded in Israel in 2018, offering custody, wallet, transfer and tokenisation technology to banks, exchanges, payment firms and crypto businesses worldwide. It says it has secured trillions of dollars in transfers for over 2,000 customers. It raised $550m in 2022 at an $8bn valuation. Private. B2B crypto infrastructure, well known in digital asset circles but not to the public.

Harness is a San Francisco software delivery platform, founded by Jyoti Bansal, that supplies AI-assisted CI/CD, feature flags, cloud cost management, security testing and internal developer portals to engineering teams. Customers include thousands of enterprises, and it raised $240m in 2025 at a $5.5bn valuation, with total funding of around $815m. Private. B2B developer brand with no consumer awareness; sponsors some developer and sports events.

Match Group is a Dallas-based (listing shows Los Angeles) online dating company, operating Tinder, Hinge, Match.com, OkCupid, Plenty of Fish, Meetic and Azar, with tens of millions of paying users and revenue near $3.5bn from subscriptions and in-app purchases. Spun off from IAC in 2020 and listed on Nasdaq (MTCH). Very strong consumer brands, particularly Tinder and Hinge, and active in marketing and event partnerships.

ClickUp is a San Diego cloud work management platform for tasks, docs, chat, goals and AI tools, used by teams from start-ups to enterprises, with millions of users globally. It earns subscription fees and was valued at $4bn after a 2021 round, with total funding of about $660m from investors including Insight Partners, Craft and Tiger Global. Founded 2017. Private. Known to knowledge workers; B2B-leaning brand with low mainstream awareness.

Quantum Lending Solutions is a Reston, Virginia fintech providing AI-powered lending technology, according to Crunchbase, presumably serving lenders with digital loan origination and servicing tools. The input shows funding of about $658m with the latest round in November 2025. It is a private B2B vendor, with little consumer awareness. Limited detail on customers or ownership is available from the input.

about: Cruise was a San Francisco autonomous vehicle company majority-owned by General Motors, operating driverless robotaxi services in San Francisco, Austin, Phoenix and other US cities until 2023. After an October 2023 accident and regulatory fallout, operations were suspended, and in December 2024 GM said it would stop funding Cruise's robotaxi work and fold it into GM. Investors included Honda, SoftBank and Microsoft, with funding near $23bn. Effectively wound down, with no commercial relevance as a sponsor.

Project Sopaipilla Holdings is described in Crunchbase as a joint venture involving Meta Platforms, likely a financing vehicle for a large AI data center campus, with about $12.5bn of funding in July 2026. It is a project-finance holding, not an operating consumer business, and the input provides no HQ. Likely B2B infrastructure funding with no consumer brand. Limited detail beyond the input.

about: AppLovin is a Palo Alto software company whose AXON AI advertising engine matches mobile app and e-commerce advertisers with ad inventory, with a legacy portfolio of mobile games now sold to Tripledot. It earns ad network fees from advertisers and publishers, and revenue has grown to around $5bn with high margins. Listed on Nasdaq (APP) and in the S&P 500. B2B ad-tech with little consumer awareness, though well known with investors.

Liquid Intelligent Technologies is a pan-African technology group, with its registered office in Mauritius, and operations run by Strive Masiyiwa's Econet. It provides fibre networks, cloud, cybersecurity, data center and connectivity services to enterprises, governments and telecoms across Africa through brands such as Liquid Cloud and Africa Data Centres, with Cassava Technologies as parent. Private, with funding from development banks. B2B, known to African enterprises and little to consumers.

MKS Instruments is an Andover, Massachusetts supplier of instruments, subsystems and process control solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, electronics, advanced materials and life sciences, including vacuum, laser, photonics and power products, many from its 2016 acquisition of Newport and 2022 Atotech deal. Revenue is near $3.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (MKSI). B2B industrial technology brand, with no consumer awareness.

Mobileye is an Israeli driver-assistance and autonomous driving technology company, headquartered in Jerusalem, whose EyeQ chips and vision software are fitted in tens of millions of cars from automakers such as Volkswagen, Ford, BMW and Nissan. It also develops robotaxi and self-driving systems. Intel acquired it in 2017 and relisted it on Nasdaq (MBLY) in 2022, retaining majority ownership. B2B technology supplier, with strong awareness in automotive circles and little among consumers.

Yinwang Smart Technology (Yinwang Intelligent Technology, Shenzhen Yinwang) is Huawei's intelligent automotive solutions business, created in 2023 as a Huawei subsidiary to supply ADS driver assistance, HarmonyOS cockpits and electric drive systems to Chinese carmakers for HIMA vehicles such as Aito, Luxeed, Stelato and Maextro. Changan Automobile bought a 10 percent stake in 2024 for CNY 11.5bn. Private. A technology supplier, with strong consumer awareness because of the Huawei brand in China.

Dayforce (formerly Ceridian) is a Minneapolis-based cloud human capital management software company, supplying payroll, HR, time and attendance, benefits and talent tools to mid-market and large employers in North America and abroad. Revenue is above $1.8bn. Thoma Bravo agreed to take it private in 2025 in an $12.3bn deal, after which it left the NYSE (DAY). B2B software with solid HR industry recognition, and little consumer awareness.

America Movil is a Mexico City-based mobile and fixed telecom giant controlled by Carlos Slim's family, with about 300 million wireless subscribers in Mexico (Telcel), Brazil (Claro), Colombia, Argentina, Chile, Central America and parts of Europe (A1, Telekom Austria). Revenue is about $50bn. Listed on the Mexican exchange (AMX) and NYSE. Very strong consumer brands Telcel and Claro across Latin America, with major sports sponsorships, notably in football and motorsport, including Telmex-Telcel's long F1 history with Sergio Perez.

Bridge Data Centres is a Singapore-based hyperscale data center developer and operator in Asia-Pacific, with campuses in Malaysia, Indonesia, Hong Kong, China, India, Thailand, Australia and Japan, serving cloud, internet and enterprise customers. Founded in 2019, it was acquired by Bain Capital and is a standalone brand. Private, with funding of about $2.8bn. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

Caris Life Sciences is an Irving, Texas AI-enabled precision medicine company providing molecular profiling of tumours, with whole exome and transcriptome sequencing, to guide cancer treatment choices for oncologists and biopharma partners. It generated revenue above $400m before its June 2025 IPO on Nasdaq (CAI). Founded by David Halbert. Customers are hospitals, doctors and drug developers. Mostly B2B and clinician-facing, with modest direct consumer awareness.

Celonis is a Munich and New York process mining and execution management software company, helping large organisations analyse how business processes run and fix inefficiencies using its Process Intelligence platform. Customers include Siemens, Uber, Coca-Cola and other large enterprises. It was valued at $13bn in 2022, with total funding around $2.4bn from Accel, 83North and Arena Holdings. Private. B2B software well known to IT leaders and consultants, with little consumer awareness, though it is a known sports sponsor.

Check Point Software Technologies is a cybersecurity company founded in Israel, with US headquarters in Redwood City and its main office in Tel Aviv, selling network firewalls, cloud security, endpoint, email and threat prevention products (Quantum, Harmony, CloudGuard) to over 100,000 organisations. Revenue is about $2.6bn. Listed on Nasdaq (CHKP). B2B brand with strong IT security recognition, and sponsorship activity including a long-running Formula 1 relationship with Scuderia Ferrari-related partners in the past.

Clio is a Burnaby, British Columbia cloud legal practice management software company, serving law firms with case management, billing, client intake and AI tools (Clio Manage, Clio Grow, Clio Work), with over 150,000 users. It raised $900m in 2025 at a $5bn valuation and agreed to buy vLex for about $1bn. Founded in 2008. Private. B2B software with strong awareness among lawyers and little in the general public.

Gigaclear is a UK full-fibre broadband provider based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, building gigabit networks in rural villages and small towns and selling broadband to homes and businesses, and wholesale. Revenue is under GBP 100m, with debt financing and equity from investors including Infracapital (M&G) and Universities Superannuation Scheme. Private. Regional consumer broadband brand, with limited national awareness.

Lowell Group is a UK-based credit management company, from Leeds, which buys and collects consumer debt, owning brands such as Lowell, Fredrikson & Associates and Carrington Law, with operations in the UK, Germany, the Nordics and the Netherlands. It serves banks, utilities and telecoms, earning recoveries. Owned by Permira and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan after a 2017-18 buyout. Private. B2B debt purchaser with low consumer brand goodwill.

Quantum Computing Inc. is a Hoboken, New Jersey company, listed on Nasdaq (QUBT), developing photonic quantum technologies such as thin-film lithium niobate chips and quantum optics for sensing, computing and security. It has raised capital through private placements, giving it a cash pile near $1.5bn. Revenue is tiny. Speculative technology company with a strong retail-investor following but no consumer products.

RingCentral is a Belmont, California cloud communications company providing business phone, video meetings (RingEX), contact centre and AI tools, for companies of all sizes, with revenue near $2.4bn. Customers range from small businesses to large enterprises, paying subscription fees. Listed on the NYSE (RNG). B2B brand with strong awareness among IT buyers, plus sports sponsorship including the Rocket Mortgage-style naming deals and NASCAR in the past.

Rippling is a San Francisco workforce management platform combining HR, payroll, IT device management, spend and benefits in one system, serving tens of thousands of businesses, from start-ups to mid-size firms. Founded in 2016 by Parker Conrad, it raised $450m in 2025 at a $16.8bn valuation, led by Elad Gil and Baillie Gifford. Private. B2B software with high recognition among HR and start-up leaders, and an active marketing and sponsorship presence in sports, including with F1 teams.

S&P Global is a New York financial data and analytics group, owning S&P Global Ratings, S&P Global Market Intelligence, S&P Dow Jones Indices (the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average), Platts and Mobility (including CARFAX), and reporting revenue near $14bn. Customers are investors, banks, corporates and governments. Listed on the NYSE (SPGI). Strong B2B brand, with the S&P 500 known to the public, and sponsors in finance and sport.

TierPoint is a St. Louis-based US data center and cloud services provider offering colocation, managed hosting, disaster recovery and cybersecurity from about 30 data centers, serving mid-market enterprises. It is backed by Brightstar and Wafra, with large debt facilities (raised $2.4bn including financing), and acquired several smaller operators. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

WeRide is an autonomous driving company founded in China and now with a San Jose and Guangzhou presence, developing robotaxis, robobuses, robovans and driver assistance, with operations in China, the UAE, Singapore and Europe, with partners such as Uber, Nissan and Renault. It listed on Nasdaq (WRD) in 2024 and later added a Hong Kong listing. Funding is about $1.8bn. B2B and fleet-oriented, with growing visibility in the UAE and Chinese cities.

Paxos is a New York blockchain infrastructure company and regulated trust company founded in 2012. It issues regulated stablecoins, including Pax Dollar (USDP), PayPal's PYUSD and Global Dollar (USDG), and provides tokenization, crypto brokerage and custody infrastructure to banks, fintechs and asset managers such as PayPal, Interactive Brokers and Mastercard. Chartered by the New York Department of Financial Services. B2B infrastructure, known mainly in finance and crypto, with limited consumer awareness.

Yendo is a Dallas, Texas fintech offering consumer credit cards, notably the Yendo Card, aimed at car owners who borrow against the value of their vehicle to build credit. Customers are US consumers, many with limited credit history; it earns interest and fees. Founded by Jimmy Jones and others, it has raised significant debt and equity financing, with a reported total of about $507 million. Early-stage consumer finance brand with limited awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Yendo offers a suite of consumer credit cards

about: Nothing is a London-based consumer electronics company founded in 2020 by Carl Pei, co-founder of OnePlus. It makes Nothing Phone smartphones, Nothing Ear and CMF by Nothing audio and wearables, known for transparent design and its Glyph light interface, and is building AI-led devices and the Essential feature in its OS. Sells directly and through retail partners in dozens of markets, mainly Europe, India and the US. It has raised about $450 million. Growing design-led consumer brand with strong youth and tech awareness.

SK Horizon is a Seoul-based AI data center infrastructure company (AIDC). The Crunchbase description says it is an AI data center infrastructure company, with an unusually large reported funding figure (about 3.08 trillion Korean won, August 2026). It is likely related to the SK Group, but ownership and details are not confirmed by the input. B2B infrastructure. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: SK Horizon is an Al data center (AIDC) infrastructure company.

about: Turkcell is Turkey's largest mobile operator, headquartered in Istanbul, offering mobile, fixed broadband, TV and digital services such as BiP messaging, fizy, and Paycell, plus subsidiaries in Ukraine and Belarus. Serves roughly 40 million subscribers in Turkey. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (TCELL) and NYSE (TKC); a major shareholder is the Turkey Wealth Fund. Very high consumer brand awareness in Turkey and a sponsor of football (Turkcell Super Lig naming rights historically) and other sports.

Wistron Corporation is a Taipei-based electronics manufacturing and design company, founded in 2001 as a spin-off of Acer. It builds laptops, servers, networking and medical equipment for brands such as Dell, HP and Lenovo, plus AI servers via the Wiwynn subsidiary. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (3231) with revenue in the tens of billions of dollars. B2B contract manufacturing, little consumer brand awareness.

Wiwynn is a Taipei-based cloud computing and data center hardware company, founded in 2012 as a subsidiary of Wistron. It designs and manufactures servers, storage and rack-scale systems for hyperscale cloud providers such as Microsoft, Meta and Google, including AI servers. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (6669). B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Flex (Flex Ltd.) is a global contract electronics manufacturer and supply chain company, historically Flextronics, with operational headquarters in Austin, Texas and legal home in Singapore. It designs and manufactures products for automotive, healthcare, industrial, communications and data center clients, including power and cooling for AI data centers, with about $26 billion revenue and some 150,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (FLEX). B2B, low brand awareness among consumers.

Alan is a Paris-based French digital health insurance company founded in 2016 by Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve and Charles Gorintin. It provides health insurance and healthcare services to companies and their employees, with a mobile app, and has expanded into Spain, Belgium and Canada. It holds a French insurance licence and serves hundreds of thousands of members. Raised about $1.2 billion in total with a valuation of roughly 4 billion euros. Well-known startup brand in France.

Bell Canada, often simply Bell, is a Montreal-based telecommunications company and the largest in Canada, part of BCE Inc. (TSX/NYSE: BCE). It offers wireless, internet, TV (Fibe), landline and business network services, plus Bell Media (CTV, TSN, Crave) through its parent. It serves over 22 million subscriber connections. Very high consumer brand awareness in Canada and a major sports sponsor, including NHL, NFL broadcast rights and the Canadian Grand Prix.

Bird is the Amsterdam-based cloud communications platform formerly called MessageBird, founded in 2011 by Robert Vis. It provides APIs and software for SMS, voice, WhatsApp and email messaging, a customer-engagement inbox and a conversational AI offering, serving thousands of businesses worldwide.
